page: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-intel is an entry-tier virtual instance within the High Performance lineup, offering 2 shared vCPUs derived from a single physical Intel Xeon core operating at 2.0 GHz with hyperthreading. The compute configuration is supported by 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 16 MB of L3 cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and vector instruction extensions such as AVX-512F and AVX-512_VNNI, alongside AES encryption acceleration. Graphics processing hardware is absent, while local primary storage includes a bundled 100 GB NVMe SSD and a single public IPv4 address.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate modest computational and memory subsystem performance consistent with a shared-core hyperthreaded setup. Single-core performance achieves a Geekbench score of 1167.0, placing it within the middle 50% tier, while multi-core metrics fall into lower percentiles with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2057.0 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 2729.87. Uncached memory throughput measures 11.67 GB/sec for sequential reads and 9.16 GB/sec for writes, leading to lower-tier PassMark memory and database scores. Static web serving throughput reaches 2.96 GB/sec, and in-memory Redis SET operations achieve 2.57 million operations per second.

The qualitative value of this configuration rests on its low infrastructure resource consumption combined with integrated high-speed NVMe storage. Because the physical core is shared, raw execution speed and throughput are constrained under sustained multi-threaded contention. Workloads best suited for this instance include lightweight web hosting, development or staging environments, entry-level continuous integration tasks, utility scripts, and low-traffic back-end services that do not require dedicated compute guarantees.
description: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-intel is a virtual server instance powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor. The configuration allocates 2 shared vCPUs across one hyperthreaded physical core clocked at 2.0 GHz, matched with 4.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 100 GB NVMe SSD. It features AVX-512 vector support and integrated cryptographic flags, though dedicated GPU acceleration is omitted. Performance testing shows average single-core Geekbench results of 1167.0, alongside lower-tier multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics resulting from its shared physical resource footprint. The instance provides a practical resource balance for utility microservices, staging setups, lightweight static web servers, and low-scale application backends requiring fast local SSD storage without intensive CPU demands.
